newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thomson plant headed for closure, despite protests.
newsitem.headline: Thomson plant headed for closure, despite protests.

text.p: Union demonstrations on Wednesday failed to reverse a decision by Television Germany GmbH to shut down a plant in northern Germany, local politicians said.

"The decision of the French is definitive," said Gerhard Schroeder, premier of the state of Lower Saxony, who negotiated a layoff benefit plan with managers of French parent Thomson SA in Paris on Tuesday.
The closing of the television plant eliminated 650 jobs only a week after Bonn said German unemployment surged in January to 4.66 million, its highest level since 1933.
Schroeder said talks were continuing about a possible management buyout of a Thomson plastics factory nearby in Celle, a move that would save jobs for some of its 150 workers.
Members of the IG Metall metal and engineering union demonstrated in Hanover and Celle in an effort to push Thomson to reconsider.
Thomson planned to close the Hanover television plant because of high production costs. Two weeks ago workers laid down tools temporarily to protest against the plan.
